4. Controller, jam response and power loss
The observation-driven sequence

The controller receives observations and its command history:

Source wrench and relative pose.
Individual leg-force readings.
Complete-profile minima, validity and timestamps.
Side-clearance evidence.
Transport-key and keeper witnesses.
Replacement identity, penetration, retention and preload.
Actuator effort and travel.
Receiver clearances, rack state and tool-clear state.

Fault labels remain in the simulated plant. The observations themselves are generated by introduced plant laws; they are not measured images or physical lock responses.

The sequence is:

Dock while the original connection remains intact.
Establish every temporary attachment and close both cuts.
Progressively transfer load to the bypass.
Mechanically retain the drives.
Release and physically separate the original connection.
Install the replacement and inspect its positive engagement.
Return the load progressively.
Freeze the main drives mechanically.
Open and inspect one selected cut in each leg.
Recover a jam through the independent keeper and second cut.
Perform provisional qualification.
Retrieve the paired cassettes through the explicit support relay.
Inspect the replacement under the intended wrench with all temporary machinery clear.
Restore the rack and both release stages before declaring completion.

A useful control correction emerged from the coupled model: drive recentering must occur only after the selected cuts are captured again. The controller records the imbalance between opposing optical corridors, closes the cuts, adjusts the drive, relocks it and then reopens for a fresh observation.

Every change in proof wrench repeats that operation. An old gap certificate is not carried across a load change.

Finite fault envelope
Observed condition	Proposed response
Short penetration, missing retention or false apparent seating	Retain bypass; remove and replace the rejected component
A fails to open, or stops partly open	Install independent A keeper at actual position; verify it; open B
Invalid or contaminated optical evidence	Retain support; clean and repeat reference observation
Observed side bridge	Retain support; remove the bridge; reinspect
Seized original fastener	Locally capture its preload; use paid relief tooling
